title: Enterprise capacity commitments: SLA sizing, GPU tiering & scaling policy intake
creator: Maya Chen
description: Intake and prioritize a set of enterprise requests for Dedicated capacity commitments. Customers are asking for explicit SLA targets (availability and tail latency), reserved throughput guarantees, and the ability to specify GPU class and burst policies. This ticket is the product triage to: 1) gather canonical customer asks and quantify needs, 2) evaluate trade-offs between fixed commitments vs flexible burst, 3) propose a prioritized set of negotiated SLA / capacity features with risk and engineering estimates for DRI review.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical intake spreadsheet with 12 enterprise customers summarizing requested SLA targets, peak qps, model families, and preferred GPU classes
Proposed SLA menu with 3 commitment tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) including availability SLOs, p95/p99 latency targets, reserved throughput, and burst rules
Clear engineering estimates for implementing each tier (complexity, eng points, infra cost delta) and one recommended pilot customer
Documented fallbacks and escalation path for capacity shortfalls (automatic model fallback, cross-region routing, and credit/penalty model)
Stakeholder alignment recorded (legal, sales, infra, reliability) with sign-off from infra and sales leadership
notes: Background: Multiple AE/SE teams reported customers with steady-state throughput needs of 500-5k qps and strict tail latency targets (p99 < 300ms) for chat workloads. Customers prefer guaranteed reserved throughput for business SLAs.

Key tension: Reserved capacity reduces customer variability risk but increases Redwood committed spend. Alternatives include negotiated burst budgets, priority queuing, or hybrid reserved+burst models.

GPU class asks: Customers are asking to specify class (e.g., H100/H200 vs A100 vs L4) for predictable latency and model compatibility. Need to evaluate procurement cost delta and slot multiplexing complexity.

Scaling policies under consideration: cold-start capacity vs warm standby; predictive scaling based on traffic forecasts; soft-reservation where reserved capacity can be borrowed by other customers with preemption and credits.

Legal & Sales constraints: SLA credits must be simple to compute and auditable. Sales wants clear pricing multipliers for each tier and GPU class to include in contracts. Legal flagged telemetry/audit requirements for credits and breach definitions.

tradeoffs_considered: Fixed reservations provide predictability but require material idle capacity in off-peak leading to higher unit costs
Burst budgets reduce committed spend but complicate fairness; requires strong monitoring and preemption rules
Allowing GPU-class selection increases contract clarity but constrains packing and bin-packing optimization on infra side
Stricter SLA latency targets push toward higher-tier GPUs (H100/H200) or replication, increasing price — may be acceptable for enterprise premium tiers
recommendation_summary: Create a three-tier capacity commitment product: Silver (best-effort burst), Gold (reserved throughput + soft burst), Platinum (reserved throughput + dedicated GPU class + guaranteed p99 latency)
Expose GPU-class as an opt-in add-on for Gold/Platinum with clear pricing multipliers and procurement lead times
Implement soft-reservation plumbing first (preemption with credit compensation) to reduce infra footprint while offering meaningful guarantees; evaluate hard reservations in a later phase
Pilot with two existing customers who already operate at >1k qps and have strong legal appetite for SLAs; use pilot telemetry to tune pricing and SLO thresholds
risks: Overcommitting capacity could materially increase Redwood's monthly OPEX if adoption is lower than sales forecasts
Complex contract terms (preemption, credits) may slow sales cycles unless templates are standardized
GPU-class opt-in reduces packing efficiency and may increase tail latency variability for other customers unless isolation boundaries are improved
Monitoring and attribution for SLA credits requires additional observability features (per-tenant bucketed metrics and audit logs)
stakeholders: Finance: Pricing model and revenue ops
